solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: African country falling short, so economist is needed

indicators.note: a word falling short stops before its end, so the country's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa
so and thus both mean 'therefore'

explanation.surface: An African nation's finances are failing, so an economist is called in to help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling short' drops the last letter of MALI, leaving MAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Malthus was the English economist famous for his theory of population growth outstripping food supply.

clue.text: Things bringing a profit — the little black spiders so regarded?

definitions.meaning: lucrative ventures that earn a lot of cash

definitions.text: the little black spiders so regarded?
definitions.meaning: small black money spiders are said to bring wealth to the person they run over

explanation.walkthrough: Folklore says a money spider crawling on you brings good fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucrative ventures earn plenty, and the tiny spiders are thought lucky charms for wealth.

clue.text: Groups of people — there are about nine in a marathon

definitions.text: there are about nine in a marathon
definitions.meaning: an old unit of distance of about three miles; a marathon is about 26 miles

explanation.walkthrough: An old measure of roughly three miles fits nine times into the 26.2 miles of a marathon.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is both an association of clubs or people and an archaic distance of about three miles.

clue.text: Shelter children found in cupboard?

parts.note: a hut is a simple shelter

explanation.surface: Kids discovered hiding in a cupboard for shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hutch can be a cupboard or dresser with shelves, as well as a rabbit cage.

clue.text: Frustration for someone trying to enter house in Norfolk village?

definitions.text: Frustration for someone trying to enter house
definitions.meaning: a key that will not turn easily in a lock
a village on the north Norfolk coast in eastern England

explanation.walkthrough: Stiffkey is a village on the north Norfolk coast; read as two words it is a key that will not turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiffkey names a coastal Norfolk village, and split up describes a lock-jamming key.

clue.text: Expert at handling words not so nice when spoken

indicators.note: the clue asks us to hear the word rather than read it, giving a same-sounding name

parts.note: fouler means nastier, less nice

explanation.surface: A wordsmith whose language is coarser when said out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: H. W. Fowler wrote the classic guide Modern English Usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Fowler, the lexicographer behind Modern English Usage, is the archetypal authority on correct English usage.

clue.text: Guess American weightwatcher may be worried about it?

definitions.meaning: in US usage to ... is to reckon or guess

definitions.text: weightwatcher may be worried about it?
definitions.meaning: a dieter frets about body shape

explanation.definitionFit: Americans say 'I figure' for 'I reckon', and a dieter worries about their bodily shape.

clue.text: He watered ground affected by the elements

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are broken up and remade

explanation.surface: A man watered the soil, which then suffered from wind and rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something weathered has been worn or changed by exposure to wind, rain and sun.

clue.text: Pleasure-seeker in eastern film lacking heart

indicators.note: the film word loses its central letter, its heart

parts.note: a picture is a film

explanation.surface: A hedonist appears in an oriental movie with a hollow centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking heart' removes the middle T of PICTURE.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure is a person devoted to refined sensual pleasure, especially fine food and drink.

clue.text: Dodgy event that is right under your eyes?

definitions.text: Dodgy event that is right under your eyes?

parts.words: Dodgy event that is right under your eyes?
parts.note: a close call is a dodgy moment; read literally, something right under your eyes is an object close by

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase works both as a narrow escape and, literally, as an object that is close at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape or close call is a risky event that very nearly went wrong.

clue.text: Muslim and saint among the top people

parts.note: Ali, the Prophet's son-in-law, is a common Muslim name

explanation.surface: A Muslim and a saint mixing with the elite.
explanation.definitionFit: The A-list is the top tier of celebrities, the most sought-after guests.

clue.text: When certain races take place, fast one has let rip

indicators.note: to let rip is to act wildly and without restraint, so the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A speedy horse has really cut loose in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let rip' rearranges FAST ONE HAS LET; 'let' is fodder too.
explanation.definitionFit: In British horse racing, the flat season is the period when races without jumps are run.

clue.text: Youngster, the solver I'm addressing? This is denied

parts.note: the setter speaks to the solver as 'you'

indicators.note: the word This is denied the letters of 'is', which are removed from it

parts.note: the clue's own word is supplies the letters taken away

explanation.surface: The setter teases the solver: are you a youngster? No, that is denied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'denied' removes IS from THIS, leaving TH.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth is a young person, especially an adolescent boy.

clue.text: What baker offers could make her famous

indicators.note: the letters of the following words could be rearranged to make something new

explanation.surface: A baker's speciality might win her renown.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmhouse is a traditional style of loaf sold in bakeries, so it is something a baker sells.

clue.text: Festival admission ticket a thing of the past

parts.note: a pass lets you in somewhere
something over is finished and done with

explanation.surface: A festival whose entry ticket has gone out of use.
explanation.definitionFit: Passover is the Jewish spring festival commemorating the Exodus from Egypt.

clue.text: To banish care — it's so tricky

indicators.note: something tricky is awkward or devious, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Driving away worry is hard to pull off.
explanation.definitionFit: To ostracise is to exclude someone from a group, effectively banishing them.

clue.text: Blair getting nothing right? That does surprise me!

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
'Well!' is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: An exclamation at Tony Blair getting nothing right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blair' suggests Tony Blair, but George Orwell's real name was Eric Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell was the pen name of the writer Eric Arthur Blair.

clue.text: Oppressive influence that may pose difficulty for manual worker

definitions.meaning: a stifling, deadening control, often from the past

definitions.text: that may pose difficulty for manual worker
definitions.meaning: a numb, lifeless hand would trouble someone working with their hands

explanation.definitionFit: The 'dead hand' of bureaucracy is a stifling control, and literally a lifeless hand hampers a labourer.

clue.text: Idiot in union — compassion denied one

parts.note: the NUM is Britain's National Union of Mineworkers

indicators.note: the word for compassion is denied a letter, which is taken out of it

parts.note: pity is compassion
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fool in the trade union denied any sympathy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'denied' takes I out of PITY, leaving PTY. NUMPTY is Scottish slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Numpty is informal Scottish and British slang for a stupid or foolish person.

clue.text: Artist is so devoid of love when friend comes round

indicators.note: the friend word encircles the other letters, wrapping round them

parts.note: a mate is a friend

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O, which the word so must lose

explanation.surface: An artist feels unloved until a friend visits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devoid of love' uses tennis love, zero, for the letter O, leaving a single S; 'comes round' has the friend word enclosing the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was the celebrated French painter of the Fauvist movement.

clue.text: Organised time of austerity and didn't give up

parts.note: an event held is one organised or staged
a fast is a period of going without food

explanation.surface: Someone arranged a lean period and refused to quit.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold fast is to keep a firm grip or stand firm, refusing to yield.

clue.text: Unfavourable note on bit of the Bible?

parts.note: an ad is a short notice or advertisement
a verse is a numbered division of a Bible chapter

explanation.surface: A disapproving comment written on a passage of Scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse conditions or comments are hostile or harmful, working against someone.

clue.text: Mark on church hard to find

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A blemish on a church that is difficult to spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarce goods are in short supply, rare and seldom met with.

clue.text: Opening day makes one filled with delight

parts.note: an entrance is an opening into a building

explanation.surface: The launch day leaves someone thrilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Entranced means enchanted or spellbound, charmed and delighted.

clue.text: This bank would hold student event for influence

definitions.text: This bank would hold student event for influence

parts.words: This bank would hold student event for influence
parts.note: a river embankment word that, with a student rag (a charity event) put inside it, spells a word for influence: leverage

explanation.surface: A bank stages a student function to buy influence.
explanation.walkthrough: A RAG is a British student charity event; place RAG inside this embankment word and LEVERAGE appears. The definition is 'This bank'.
explanation.definitionFit: A levee is an embankment built along a river to stop flooding, a kind of bank.

clue.text: Green areas? Any number restricted by rules here

indicators.note: the number is hemmed in by the rules word, held within it

parts.note: laws are rules
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: Parks where any number of people are bound by regulations.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawns are areas of mown grass, the green patches of a garden or park.

clue.text: Spuds regularly supplied by hospital to accompany one foreign dish

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals from the word Spuds, first, third and fifth

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Potatoes served from a hospital kitchen alongside an exotic dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish, so foreign food to British solvers.

clue.text: Dark row, so upsetting, can stop people making progress

indicators.note: the letters are upset, knocked over and jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: An angry dispute so distressing it can hold people back.
explanation.definitionFit: Repairs to a road hold up traffic, stopping travellers getting along.

clue.text: Admire one emerging from daydream

indicators.note: the letter for one comes out of the daydream word, leaving the rest

parts.note: a reverie is a daydream
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Waking from a daydream full of admiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emerging from' takes I out of REVERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere someone is to hold them in deep respect and admiration.

clue.text: Show contempt for big research organisation in notice

parts.note: to dis someone is to disrespect them
CERN is the European particle physics laboratory near Geneva

explanation.surface: A notice in which someone scorns a major scientific body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notice' looks like a noun for a sign; here it is the verb, to perceive.
explanation.definitionFit: To discern something is to perceive or make it out, to spot it.
